title: High-Concurrency Ticket Booking (BookMyShow)
intro: Design a high-concurrency ticket booking platform handling viral stadium concert sales with zero double-booking and fair virtual queuing.
objectives: Implement distributed seat holding with short-lived TTLs using Redis mutexes.
Protect primary databases during flash sales via Virtual Waiting Rooms (Token buckets).
Handle seat release timeouts when customers abandon payment checkout.
body:
### The Flash-Sale Ticket Problem
When tickets for a stadium concert go live, 500,000 fans attempt to reserve 50,000 seats in seconds. Direct database queries crash under row-lock contention.

### The Multi-Tier Architecture
1. **Virtual Waiting Room (Queue-IT)**: Incoming users enter a waiting room queue and are admitted to the seat selection canvas in metered batches matching backend processing capacity.
2. **Temporary Seat Hold (Redis Mutex with TTL)**: When Alice clicks seat `A-12`, server acquires Redis distributed lock `SET lock:seat:A12 user_alice NX EX 600` (10-minute lease).
3. **Seat State Transition**: `AVAILABLE -> HELD -> BOOKED`.
4. **Timeout Expiration**: If payment is not completed in 10 minutes, Redis key expires and seat returns to `AVAILABLE`.
keyIdea: Meter incoming flash traffic with a virtual waiting room. Use distributed Redis locks with finite leases (TTLs) to manage temporary seat holds.

concepts.title: Optimistic Locking
concepts.body: Database rows verify version number on commit (`UPDATE seat SET status='BOOKED', version=2 WHERE id='A12' AND version=1`).

concepts.title: Seat Map Caching
concepts.body: Compress stadium seat availability bitmap and distribute via CDN with short 2-second TTLs.

examples: Ticketmaster and BookMyShow handling stadium world tour drops.

quiz.prompt: Why should temporary seat holds carry a strict Time-To-Live (TTL)?
options: To automatically release seats back to other customers if a user abandons checkout without paying
To reduce network bandwidth on Wi-Fi
quiz.explanation: A TTL ensures seats locked by users who drop off or experience payment failure are automatically freed for other buyers.
